comments.author: AndrewOMartin
comments.why_zh: Python 字典实现的最新进展。
comments.quote_zh: 就我个人而言，只要标题里有“Raymond Hettinger”，任何视频我都会看。
comments.text_zh: [VIDEO] Raymond Hettinger 的 Modern Dictionaries 这个演讲的官方简介如下，但就我个人而言，只要标题里有“Raymond Hettinger”，任何视频我都会看。 > Python 的字典好得惊人。多年来，许多伟大的想法汇聚在一起，造就了 Python 3.6 中的现代实现。这场有趣的演讲由 Raymond Hettinger 主讲，他是 Python 核心开发者，负责 set 的实现，并设计了 CPython 中为 Python 3.6 实现、以及 PyPy 中为 Python 2.7 实现的紧凑且有序的 dict。他将用图片和少量纯 Python 代码来解释所有关键想法以及它们随时间演变的过程。他还会介绍较新的特性，例如 key-sharing、compaction 和 versioning。这场演讲很重要，因为它是截至 Python 3.6 关于这一最先进实现唯一公开的讨论。即便是经验丰富的 Python 用户，也未必了解最新的这些创新。
comments.text: [VIDEO] Modern Dictionaries by Raymond Hettinger The official description of this talk is below, but personally, I'd watch any video with "Raymond Hettinger" in the title. > Python's dictionaries are stunningly good. Over the years, many great ideas have combined together to produce the modern implementation in Python 3.6. This fun talk is given by Raymond Hettinger, the Python core developer responsible for the set implementation and who designed the compact-and-ordered dict implemented in CPython for Python 3.6 and in PyPy for Python 2.7. He will use pictures and little bits of pure python code to explain all of the key ideas and how they evolved over time. He will also include newer features such as key-sharing, compaction, and versioning. This talk is important because it is the only public discussion of the state of the art as of Python 3.6. Even experienced Python users are unlikely to know the most recent innovations.

comments.author: quelltext
comments.why_zh: 演讲解释了删除留下的空洞以及顺序的由来。
comments.quote_zh: 听起来是个有趣的演讲。
comments.text_zh: 这个实现是从 3.6 开始使用的，对吧？有意思的是，那封想法邮件提到，除了内存布局之外，实现没有任何变化（包括顺序）。这会意味着插入顺序在更早版本中就已经被保留了（如果我没记错，并非如此），或者这个想法后来又经历了一些确实影响顺序的改动。编辑：我没能完全找到答案，但 [LINK] 提到，这种行为从那时起就存在，因为该实现只在 hash table 本身中跟踪索引，并依赖把条目单独维护在第二个数组中，而该数组按插入顺序扩展。这看起来也挺直接，但它引出了一些问题，比如删除是如何（高效地）实现的。编辑2：好吧，演讲（[VIDEO]）提到，他们只是留下空洞，直到下一次 resize（大约在 42:00 处）。Raymond 在那里还提到，他最初的想法并不保留顺序，顺序的出现是因为额外的一项 compacting 优化？可能哪天该把整个演讲看完，弄清这段历史。听起来是个有趣的演讲。
comments.text: This implementation was used from 3.6, right? It's interesting that the idea mail mentions that nothing changes about the implementation (including order) but the memory layout. Which would imply insertion order was already preserved in older versions (not the case IIRC) or the idea underwent a few more changes that did in fact impact order. EDIT: I couldn't quite find an answer but [LINK] mentions the behavior happens since then because the implementation only tracks indices in the hash table itself and relies on maintaining entries separately in a second array that gets expanded in insertion order. This would also seem straightforward but it raises a few questions such as how deletion is implemented (efficiently). EDIT2: Okay, the talk ( [VIDEO] ) mentions they just leave holes until the next resize (at around 42:00). Raymond also mentions there that his original idea didn't preserve ordering but happened due to an additional compacting optimization? Should probably watch the whole thing some time to get the history. Sounds like a fun talk.

comments.author: Rendello
comments.why_zh: 引用来说明 Python dict 顺序的历史。
comments.text_zh: 我本来想半开玩笑地建议把未定义行为随机化，但我想这在调试中很常见，甚至在一些 API 里也能见到。曾经在 Python 中，dictionary（hashmap）的顺序被随机化，这样用户就不会依赖未指定的顺序行为。不过最终，dictionary 被保证保持插入顺序。[VIDEO]
comments.text: I was going to make a tongue-in-cheek suggestion about randomizing undefined behaviour, but I suppose that's common in debugging and even seen in some APIs. At one time, in Python, dictionary (hashmap) ordering was randomized so users wouldn't rely on non-specified ordering behaviour. Eventually though, dictionaries were guaranteed insertion ordering. [VIDEO]

comments.author: Spivak
comments.story_title: Are Python Dictionaries Ordered Data Structures?
comments.why_zh: 引用来说明 Python dict 的质量和受关注程度。
comments.text_zh: Python 的 dict() 已经是高质量、高性能的。你大概没法比现状做得更好多少。如果想要更快，最终就得把数据移到一种允许你做出更多假设、对数据施加更多限制并在那里操作数据的环境里。numpy、polaris 和 pandas 就是这么工作的。Python 里一切都是 dict，没有哪种数据结构得到过比它更多的关注。[VIDEO]
comments.text: The python dict() is already high-quality and high-performance. You're probably not going to be able to do much better than the current state. If you want faster you end up moving your data into an environment that lets you make more assumptions and be more restrictive with your data and operate on it there. It's how numpy, polaris, and pandas work. Everything in Python is a dict, there's no data structure that's been given more attention. [VIDEO]

comments.author: aewens

comments.quote_zh: 他做过一个很有名的演讲，叫
comments.text_zh: 我认为这里特别提到 Raymond Hettinger，是因为他做过一个很有名的演讲，叫 [Modern Dictionaries]( [VIDEO] )，在大概 32:00 到 35:00 处，他打趣说，年轻开发者以为需要新的数据结构来处理新问题，但最终只是重新创造/重新发现 1960 年代的解决方案。“已有的事后必再有，已行的事后必再行；日光之下并无新事。”
comments.text: I think Raymond Hettinger is called out specially here because he did a well known talk called [Modern Dictionaries]( [VIDEO] ) where around 32:00 to 35:00 in he makes the quip about how younger developers think they need new data structures to handle new problems, but eventually just end up recreating / rediscovering solutions from the 1960s. “What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done; there is nothing new under the sun.”
